title: Bi-Encoders: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Two Towers, One Score | the query vector q is dragged against three precomputed document vectors d1, d2, d3, with a corpus-size control comparing bi-encoder work against cross-encoder work | encoding the two sides separately means request-time cost is one query encoding plus comparisons instead of one transformer pass per pair, and the document vectors are never recomputed

2. Pooling And Padding | mean pooling over token states h1, h2, h3 with 0 to 5 padding vectors wrongly included, toggling between zero and realistic non-zero padding states | pooling turns token embeddings into one sentence embedding, and unmasked padding shrinks the vector to [0.225, 0.225] or moves its direction, degrading the index while nothing errors

3. MaxSim Late Interaction | a tappable 2x3 similarity grid between two query tokens and three document tokens, with the max-per-query-token sum recomputed live | keeping token embeddings lets each query concept find its own supporting token for a MaxSim of 0.9 + 0.8 = 1.7, which one pooled vector cannot express

4. Bytes Per Chunk | two dials over vectors per chunk and dimensions per vector, showing bytes per chunk and the total for ten million chunks | vectors x dimensions x 4 bytes is the whole cost model, so 768-dim single vectors need 30.72 GB while 128 token vectors of 128 dims cost 65,536 bytes per chunk, 128x the floor

5. When Metrics Disagree | candidate a is stretched in magnitude against a fixed b while dot product, cosine and Euclidean distance each pick a winner, with a normalisation toggle | the three metrics rank differently for arbitrary vectors and identically for unit vectors, because ||x-y||^2 = 2 - 2 x.y once both norms are 1, and cosine is undefined at zero norm
